title: I Used the Company Slack No-Politics Rule on the CEO Thread

parts.text: I opened Slack at 8:44 a.m. to a CEO thread in #general endorsing a city council candidate and telling us to "vote like owners." The employee handbook, page 19, said no political campaigning on company channels. I was twenty-six, junior analyst, holding a coffee that had gone cool. I replied with a screenshot of page 19 and the words: noting for consistency. The reactions were a funeral. My manager pinged me to take it down. I did not post more. I archived the thread. Then HR posted a reminder about the handbook... attached to a smiley that linked back to the CEO's first message.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: HR reminded us of the rule while smiling at the CEO's campaign post.

social.video_title: The CEO campaigned in #general under a no-politics rule — Part 1/2
social.description: Page 19, a cool coffee, and a handbook that suddenly had a wink. Would you have replied in-thread?

parts.text: I forwarded the archive and the HR reminder to the ethics mailbox, which exists because investors like mailboxes. The CEO thread was locked. A real reminder went out without a smiley. I was not fired. I was also not promoted that cycle, which I logged as information. Page 19 stayed. #general went back to birthday bots. I drink hotter coffee now and I still know how to screenshot a PDF. Owners vote at home. Employees post GIFs of dogs.

social.video_title: Ethics locked the thread the smiley tried to save — Part 2/2
social.description: Investor mailbox, locked #general, birthday bots restored. Was a candidate a KPI?
